bull_bear.body: Construction project risks, market competition, and regulatory changes
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: The company's credit rating is an important indicator of its creditworthiness and ability to secure funding for future projects.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Track record of delivering complex, prestigious engineering projects and landmark developments, including Central Vista buildings, hospitals, hostels and universities
- Turnkey solutions for large-scale, complex projects with a robust domestic presence
- Well-diversified order book across public and private sectors, together with expanding geographical presence
- Continued investments in mechanisation, digitalisation and process excellence that enhance productivity and reduce dependence on manual labour
- Inclusion of escalation clauses in most contracts, mitigating the impact of input-cost inflation
- Prudent balance sheet, with net worth crossing the milestone of Rs 2,000 crore as on March 31, 2026
- In-house Water Technology Centre supporting low-cost, sustainable water solutions
- Strong safety record, evidenced by multiple CIDC Vishwakarma Awards 2025 for Best HSE Practices and Best Project across sites
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Labour availability and workforce shortages — The industry faced labour shortages following elections in several states during FY26; the business also cites workforce shortages as an industry-specific challenge. Mitigation is continued investment in mechanisation to reduce dependence on manual labour.
- Input-cost inflation and cost escalation — Persistent inflationary pressures on input costs affected the operating environment in FY26, alongside cost escalations flagged as an industry-specific challenge; the inclusion of escalation clauses in most contracts is the stated mitigant.
- Regulatory / environmental construction restrictions — NGT-related construction restrictions in the NCR curtailed activity during the year. Exposure is partly buffered because a significant portion of the NCR order book comprises strategic projects such as Central Vista that are not affected by such restrictions.
- Supply chain disruption from geopolitical developments — Supply chain disruptions arising from geopolitical developments in the Gulf region affected FY26 operations; heightened risks across energy markets and international trade corridors contribute to commodity price volatility and cross-border logistics disruption.
- Single-activity and single-sector concentration — Building construction accounts for 100% of turnover and construction/maintenance of buildings (NIC 4100/4220) for 98.99%, with exports at just 0.06% of turnover — leaving the Company almost entirely exposed to Indian building construction demand.
- Dependence on government and public capital expenditure — The customer base is weighted to Government authorities, Central and State Government departments and PSUs, and the demand narrative rests on elevated public capital expenditure (more than 5% of GDP) and Union Budget infrastructure allocations — making order inflow sensitive to fiscal and policy shifts.
- Information technology and cyber security risk — IT risks span security (unauthorised access to business-critical data), availability (outage of key infrastructure), performance and compliance; consequences identified include monetary loss, compromise of customer data, halt in operations, compliance violations and reputational damage. The Company sustains investments in cybersecurity and enterprise standardisation.
- Occupational health and safety exposure at project sites — Large-scale construction across 53 project sites with a workforce of nearly 20,000 non-permanent workers carries high-consequence safety risk; the Company runs an ISO 45001:2018-aligned management system with digitised risk registers and SHE Department oversight under the Whole-time Managing Director.

business.body: ACIL is an EPC company engaged in the construction of buildings — residential and commercial complexes, IT parks, institutional buildings, hospitals, corporate offices, metro stations and depots, industrial buildings and townships, BOT projects and urban infrastructure. Its capabilities span civil engineering, high-rise buildings, design-and-build projects, Build-Operate-Transfer projects and specialised infrastructure developments. It caters primarily to institutional and corporate customers, including Government authorities, Central and State Government departments, PSUs, private companies, real estate developers and other institutional clients.

outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: ACIL's expansion is project-footprint led rather than plant-capacity led. As at FY26 the Company operated from 53 project sites and 4 offices in India across 16 states, plus one international project site. Execution ramp-up during the year centred on the redevelopment of CSMT Station, which gathered significant momentum following design approvals, and the Central Vista Design-Build Project awarded in January 2026, which has entered the execution phase and is expected to contribute meaningfully to revenues in the coming quarters. Work on the DLF Dahlias project is progressing steadily and provides revenue visibility for FY27, while the Indian Jewellery Park project is in the design phase with on-ground execution expected to commence by the end of Q1 FY27. Among airport projects, Varanasi Airport is expected to be completed ahead of schedule, Darbhanga Airport during the current year, and the design process for the recently awarded Kota Airport project is underway with construction expected to commence over the next few months. The Company continues to invest selectively in advanced equipment and technology and in mechanisation and digitalisation to enhance execution capability, and is evaluating advanced construction technologies widely adopted in developed markets to improve standardisation and productivity. Environment-related capital expenditure accounted for 1.4% of total capex in FY 2025-26 (0.3% in FY 2024-25), covering energy-efficient electrical devices and equipment, anti-collision systems, smog guns and dust collection systems, RO, STP and other water treatment plants, and DG sets conforming to CPCB Stage-VI emission norms.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Infrastructure remained central to India's growth strategy in FY 2026, with the Union Budget for 2026-27 raising public expenditure to Rs 12.2 lakh crore
- Public capital expenditure in India remains elevated at more than 5% of GDP, with continued focus on infrastructure development and defence
- Key demand segments cited include upgradation of Indian railway stations, hospitals, residential complexes under Prime Minister and State Government schemes, technical institutional buildings, university/college infrastructure and Central Vista projects
- As per ICRA, India's construction sector is expected to grow 8-10% in revenue in FY27, against 6-8% growth in FY26
- India recorded an estimated 7.5% growth in FY2025-26, with real GDP growth projected at 6.7% in FY2026-27
- Continued public investment, supportive government policies, improved logistics, easier access to formal finance and a more efficient regulatory environment create significant opportunities for organised infrastructure developers
- Management expects many FY26 headwinds — labour shortages after state elections, input-cost inflation, Gulf-related supply chain disruption and NGT construction restrictions in the NCR — to ease, aided by improved political stability across key markets after FY26 elections
- A significant portion of the NCR order book comprises strategic projects such as Central Vista that are not affected by NGT restrictions
- The Water & Effluent Treatment business provides end-to-end water management solutions to government and private clients, supported by an in-house Water Technology Centre; the Middle East saw robust growth driven by desalination investment and smart water technologies
- As on March 31, 2026, the net order book stood at Rs 21,096.31 crore, providing strong revenue visibility over the next couple of years
- During FY26 the Company secured fresh orders worth Rs 10,257.39 crore
- The Company is currently the L1 bidder for two projects with a combined value of Rs 1,620.95 crore
- The order book is well-diversified across public and private sectors, with an expanding geographical presence
- Redevelopment of the CSMT Station gathered significant momentum during the year following design approvals and project ramp-up
- The Central Vista Design-Build Project, awarded in January 2026, has entered the execution phase and is expected to contribute meaningfully to revenues in the coming quarters
- Work on the DLF Dahlias project is progressing steadily, providing healthy revenue visibility for FY27

The rating reaffirmation is a positive indicator of the company's creditworthiness.

The Company continues to invest selectively in advanced equipment and technology and in mechanisation and digitalisation to enhance execution capability, and is evaluating advanced construction technologies widely adopted in developed markets to improve standardisation and productivity. Environment-related capital expenditure accounted for 1.4% of total capex in FY 2025-26 (0.3% in FY 2024-25), covering energy-efficient electrical devices and equipment, anti-collision systems, smog guns and dust collection systems, RO, STP and other water treatment plants, and DG sets conforming to CPCB Stage-VI emission norms.

risks.note: The industry faced labour shortages following elections in several states during FY26; the business also cites workforce shortages as an industry-specific challenge. Mitigation is continued investment in mechanisation to reduce dependence on manual labour.

Persistent inflationary pressures on input costs affected the operating environment in FY26, alongside cost escalations flagged as an industry-specific challenge; the inclusion of escalation clauses in most contracts is the stated mitigant.

NGT-related construction restrictions in the NCR curtailed activity during the year. Exposure is partly buffered because a significant portion of the NCR order book comprises strategic projects such as Central Vista that are not affected by such restrictions.

risks.risk: Supply chain disruption from geopolitical developments
risks.note: Supply chain disruptions arising from geopolitical developments in the Gulf region affected FY26 operations; heightened risks across energy markets and international trade corridors contribute to commodity price volatility and cross-border logistics disruption.

Building construction accounts for 100% of turnover and construction/maintenance of buildings (NIC 4100/4220) for 98.99%, with exports at just 0.06% of turnover — leaving the Company almost entirely exposed to Indian building construction demand.

risks.risk: Dependence on government and public capital expenditure
risks.note: The customer base is weighted to Government authorities, Central and State Government departments and PSUs, and the demand narrative rests on elevated public capital expenditure (more than 5% of GDP) and Union Budget infrastructure allocations — making order inflow sensitive to fiscal and policy shifts.

risks.risk: Information technology and cyber security risk
risks.note: IT risks span security (unauthorised access to business-critical data), availability (outage of key infrastructure), performance and compliance; consequences identified include monetary loss, compromise of customer data, halt in operations, compliance violations and reputational damage. The Company sustains investments in cybersecurity and enterprise standardisation.

risks.risk: Occupational health and safety exposure at project sites
risks.note: Large-scale construction across 53 project sites with a workforce of nearly 20,000 non-permanent workers carries high-consequence safety risk; the Company runs an ISO 45001:2018-aligned management system with digitised risk registers and SHE Department oversight under the Whole-time Managing Director.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Ahluwalia Contracts (India) Limited is a leading engineering, procurement and construction company executing prestigious and complex building and urban-infrastructure projects across 16 states of India.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: ACIL is an EPC company engaged in the construction of buildings — residential and commercial complexes, IT parks, institutional buildings, hospitals, corporate offices, metro stations and depots, industrial buildings and townships, BOT projects and urban infrastructure. Its capabilities span civil engineering, high-rise buildings, design-and-build projects, Build-Operate-Transfer projects and specialised infrastructure developments. It caters primarily to institutional and corporate customers, including Government authorities, Central and State Government departments, PSUs, private companies, real estate developers and other institutional clients.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Infrastructure remained central to India's growth strategy in FY 2026, with the Union Budget for 2026-27 raising public expenditure to Rs 12.2 lakh crore
- Public capital expenditure in India remains elevated at more than 5% of GDP, with continued focus on infrastructure development and defence
- Key demand segments cited include upgradation of Indian railway stations, hospitals, residential complexes under Prime Minister and State Government schemes, technical institutional buildings, university/college infrastructure and Central Vista projects
- As per ICRA, India's construction sector is expected to grow 8-10% in revenue in FY27, against 6-8% growth in FY26
- India recorded an estimated 7.5% growth in FY2025-26, with real GDP growth projected at 6.7% in FY2026-27
- Continued public investment, supportive government policies, improved logistics, easier access to formal finance and a more efficient regulatory environment create significant opportunities for organised infrastructure developers
- Management expects many FY26 headwinds — labour shortages after state elections, input-cost inflation, Gulf-related supply chain disruption and NGT construction restrictions in the NCR — to ease, aided by improved political stability across key markets after FY26 elections
- A significant portion of the NCR order book comprises strategic projects such as Central Vista that are not affected by NGT restrictions
- The Water & Effluent Treatment business provides end-to-end water management solutions to government and private clients, supported by an in-house Water Technology Centre; the Middle East saw robust growth driven by desalination investment and smart water technologies
- As on March 31, 2026, the net order book stood at Rs 21,096.31 crore, providing strong revenue visibility over the next couple of years
- During FY26 the Company secured fresh orders worth Rs 10,257.39 crore
- The Company is currently the L1 bidder for two projects with a combined value of Rs 1,620.95 crore
- The order book is well-diversified across public and private sectors, with an expanding geographical presence
- Redevelopment of the CSMT Station gathered significant momentum during the year following design approvals and project ramp-up
- The Central Vista Design-Build Project, awarded in January 2026, has entered the execution phase and is expected to contribute meaningfully to revenues in the coming quarters
- Work on the DLF Dahlias project is progressing steadily, providing healthy revenue visibility for FY27

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: ACIL's expansion is project-footprint led rather than plant-capacity led. As at FY26 the Company operated from 53 project sites and 4 offices in India across 16 states, plus one international project site. Execution ramp-up during the year centred on the redevelopment of CSMT Station, which gathered significant momentum following design approvals, and the Central Vista Design-Build Project awarded in January 2026, which has entered the execution phase and is expected to contribute meaningfully to revenues in the coming quarters. Work on the DLF Dahlias project is progressing steadily and provides revenue visibility for FY27, while the Indian Jewellery Park project is in the design phase with on-ground execution expected to commence by the end of Q1 FY27. Among airport projects, Varanasi Airport is expected to be completed ahead of schedule, Darbhanga Airport during the current year, and the design process for the recently awarded Kota Airport project is underway with construction expected to commence over the next few months. The Company continues to invest selectively in advanced equipment and technology and in mechanisation and digitalisation to enhance execution capability, and is evaluating advanced construction technologies widely adopted in developed markets to improve standardisation and productivity. Environment-related capital expenditure accounted for 1.4% of total capex in FY 2025-26 (0.3% in FY 2024-25), covering energy-efficient electrical devices and equipment, anti-collision systems, smog guns and dust collection systems, RO, STP and other water treatment plants, and DG sets conforming to CPCB Stage-VI emission norms.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Track record of delivering complex, prestigious engineering projects and landmark developments, including Central Vista buildings, hospitals, hostels and universities
- Turnkey solutions for large-scale, complex projects with a robust domestic presence
- Well-diversified order book across public and private sectors, together with expanding geographical presence
- Continued investments in mechanisation, digitalisation and process excellence that enhance productivity and reduce dependence on manual labour
- Inclusion of escalation clauses in most contracts, mitigating the impact of input-cost inflation
- Prudent balance sheet, with net worth crossing the milestone of Rs 2,000 crore as on March 31, 2026
- In-house Water Technology Centre supporting low-cost, sustainable water solutions
- Strong safety record, evidenced by multiple CIDC Vishwakarma Awards 2025 for Best HSE Practices and Best Project across sites

themes.title: Infrastructure EPC & roads order-book conversion
themes.need: India's record capital-outlay cycle (roads, metro, marine, hydro, tunnelling) gives diversified EPC contractors multi-year visibility - AFCONS tracks a ~INR4 lakh cr pipeline (70% domestic) and targets ~INR30,000cr FY27 inflow; NCC/DBL/PNCINFRA/GRINFRA/ASHOKA/CEIGALL carry large road/HAM books; AFCONS/PATELENG/AHLUCONT/PSPPROJECT add marine, hydro and building EPC. The binding issue is execution + client-payment cycles, not order intake.
themes.driver: L1-to-firm-order conversion (AFCONS Croatia/Vadhavan, DMRC awards); NHAI/HAM award pickup; monsoon-end execution ramp.
